headline: Litigation settlement lifts profit as sales inch higher
summary_short: Dillard's Q1 FY2026 revenue rose to $1,589M (+2.7% y/y, -20.1% q/q against the holiday-heavy prior quarter), while net income jumped to $251M ($16.04 diluted EPS) largely on a $104.1M pre-tax litigation-settlement gain and 3% comparable-store sales growth.
summary_long: Comparable-store sales rose about 3%, led by home & furniture, ladies' accessories/lingerie and shoes; average ticket rose 7% while transaction count fell 3%. Retail gross margin expanded to 45.8% from 45.5% (total gross margin 44.5% vs 43.9%), aided by shoes and ladies' accessories/lingerie, partly offset by softer ladies' apparel and home & furniture. SG&A rose $22.3M to $444.0M (28.3% of sales) on higher payroll costs. Net income nearly doubled y/y to $251M ($16.04 diluted EPS), driven mainly by a $104.1M pre-tax ($79.6M after-tax) gain on a credit-card-interchange-fee litigation settlement. Construction-segment revenue fell 18% on lower activity. No share buybacks this quarter; $165.2M remains authorized. Company expects a roughly 23% FY2026 effective tax rate; no other guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Net income surged mainly on a $104.1M pre-tax credit-card-interchange-fee litigation settlement, plus 3% comparable-store sales growth and retail gross-margin expansion; SG&A rose on higher payroll costs.
Driven mainly by a $104.1 million pre-tax ($79.6 million after-tax) gain from settling a long-running credit-card interchange-fee lawsuit, plus higher retail sales and gross margin.

Comparable-store sales rose about 3%, led by home & furniture, ladies' accessories/lingerie and shoes; average ticket rose 7% while transaction count fell 3%. Construction-segment revenue fell 18% on lower construction activity.

Retail gross margin rose to 45.8% from 45.5%, on moderate gains in shoes and slight gains in ladies' accessories/lingerie, partly offset by slightly softer ladies' apparel and home & furniture margins.

The q/q decline reflects a comparison against the prior shard quarter, which corresponds to the November-January holiday period; this filing itself is labeled by the company as fiscal 2026's first quarter, so the q/q drop is seasonal, not a demand deterioration.
